decisions.body:
Framing trust (lens: what a developer does before relying on what the assistant produced) chosen; its statements are copied into the main canvas.
**By:** A. Author
**Why:** The interview guide's last section asks how outputs are validated, so this is the framing the material can answer.
**Rejected:** role (lens: what the developer takes the assistant to be, and what that makes of the developer's own work); workflow (lens: where in a task the assistant is brought in, and what makes a developer hand work over to it)
decisions.why: The interview guide's last section asks how outputs are validated, so this is the framing the material can answer.
decisions.rejected: role (lens: what the developer takes the assistant to be, and what that makes of the developer's own work); workflow (lens: where in a task the assistant is brought in, and what makes a developer hand work over to it)

decisions.body:
3.1 speaks of senior developers in general; the dataset README says all 13 participants have more than five years of experience and use an assistant daily. Does the question mean these 13 or senior developers in general?
**By:** A. Author

Developers who use an AI assistant every day say they still do not take its output on trust. The puzzle is what they do instead. [accepted, src: Interview_P05.md, src: Interview_P06.md, src: Interview_P10.md]
**By:** A. Author
**Explained:** I accept that these developers say they do not take the assistant's output on trust; what they do instead is the puzzle.
